AUGUSTA, MAINE – Today September 4, marks just 60 days until the General Election on November 3. The Office of the Secretary of State today provided an update about Maine’s election processes for this stage of the election cycle.

Key dates to know:

  • September 15 - National Voter Registration Day
  • September 19 (45 days before Election Day) - Deadline to send UOCAVA ballots to already pending requests
  • October 4 (30 days before Election Day) - In-person, no-excuse absentee voting period begins (goes through close of business in a voter's town on Thurs., October 29)
  • October 20 - Election Hero Day
  • October 27 - Mock Election Day
  • October 29 - Last day to request a no-excuse absentee ballot
  • Registration deadlines:
    • In person: Close of the polls on Election Day.
    • Registering by mail or 3rd person: Received by the voter’s town or city by close of business 21 days before Election Day. (October 13) 
    • Registering online: 5 PM on the 21st day before Election Day. (October 13)
    • Registration through the BMV: On the 7th day before Election Day. (October 27)
    • UOCAVA voters in Title 21-A section 777-A by mail or electronically: By Noon the day before Election Day (November 2)
  • Absentee ballots:
    • Requesting an absentee ballot: Absentee ballots, including accessible ballots and ballots for uniformed and overseas voters, may be requested online at maine.gov/cgi-bin/online/AbsenteeBallot/index.pl. Voters may also contact their town hall to request a ballot or submit a paper application for an absentee ballot, and the request must be received at least three business days before Election Day (October 29), unless special circumstances exist.
    • Returning an absentee ballot: Only ballots received by 8 p.m. on Election Day are counted, regardless of postmark. In many towns and cities, voters have the option of returning an absentee ballot to a secured drop box. Maine voters can track the process of their ballot at: apps.web.maine.gov/cgi-bin/online/AbsenteeBallot/ballot_status.pl.

Absentee ballot processing

Absentee ballots may be processed up to seven days before Election Day, with notice provided to the Secretary of State and political parties 30 days before Election Day. A list of municipalities which may process ballots early will be available at maine.gov/sos/elections-voting/upcoming-elections at least one week prior to the start of early processing. Absentee ballot processing is a public process which may be observed by partisan and nonpartisan observers. Early processing may happen between the hours of 7 a.m. and 9 p.m., except when an inspection is requested. At such times, processing may not begin until the inspection period has concluded. Requests for inspection of absentee ballot applications and envelopes must be submitted in writing by 4 p.m. the day before each day of early processing. If such a request is made, the ballot applications and envelopes will be available an hour before early processing is set to begin.

During absentee ballot processing, teams of two work in stages. First, the absentee voter list is marked, then the ballots and envelopes separated, and only when a sufficient quantity of ballots has amassed, are the ballots unfolded and placed into the tabulator or ballot box. Ballots and envelopes are kept secure after each day of early processing. Absentee ballots are not counted until after 8 p.m. on Election Day, just as all other ballots. Many municipalities will conduct absentee ballot processing on Election Day itself, under the same procedures. 

Ranked-Choice Voting

With declared write-in candidates in both the U.S. Senate and the Congressional District 2 races, those races will be conducted by ranked choice. The ballots will include the names of the nominees as well as a blank write-in line with columns to rank candidate preferences. The list of declared write-in candidates is posted on the Secretary of State website and will be posted in polling locations. 

Ranked-choice voting, sometimes called "instant run-off voting," allows voters to choose their candidate(s) in order of preference, by marking candidates as their first, second and/or third choice. Voters may rank as many or as few candidates as they choose. 

In ranked-choice races, to win the race outright, a candidate must receive more than 50% of the first-choice votes as counted on Election Day. If no candidate receives 50% plus one vote of the total ballots cast in a particular race, then the tabulation will proceed to Augusta for the ranked-choice tabulation. The votes are tabulated in rounds, with the lowest-ranked candidates eliminated in each round until a remaining candidate receives a majority of the votes (more than 50%). The candidate who is determined to have received the majority of the votes (more than 50%) in the final round is declared the winner. Trump International Airport (DJT), formerly Palm Beach International Airport (PBI). U.S. Secret Service (USSS) requested FAA restrict aircraft operations in the vicinity of President Trump's Florida non- Governmental property. To provide adequate safeguards for USSS to secure the non-Governmental property and safeguard USSS protectees in the interest of national security, FAA is proposing to implement Special Air Traffic Rules restricting aircraft from operating in the President Donald J. Trump International Airport Special Flight Rules Area unless certain conditions are met.

MaineCare Comprehensive Benchmarking Report Initiation Notice

Aug 31, 2026

The Department initiated a comprehensive rate benchmarking report, as required by MRS Title 22 §3173-J. Rate reform law requires that, every four years, the Department compare MaineCare rates to the rates paid by the following:

  • Medicare
  • At least five comparison Medicaid states
  • Any appropriate Maine commercial payers

Interested parties will have the opportunity for public review and comment. The final report will be available on the MaineCare Rate System Reform webpage.

For questions please contact Megan Scott, MaineCare’s Legislative and Reform Coordinator.

items.title: Safe Homes Awareness Month - September
items.content_text:
WHEREAS
, the 130th Maine Legislature unanimously passed L.D. 1861, An Act to Establish the Safe Homes Program, and as Governor, I signed the bill into law on April 7, 2022; and
WHEREAS
, this bipartisan law promotes the safe storage of prescription drugs, firearms and other dangerous weapons in homes or public spaces; and
WHEREAS
, the Safe Homes Program is an optional, voluntary grant program that builds on the work of L.D. 1140, An Act To Establish a Sales Tax Exemption for the Purchase of Firearm Safety Devices, by making storage devices, such as gun safes, more affordable for people who want to buy them; and
WHEREAS
, the Safe Homes Program Fund will provide grants for purchasing safety devices for the safe storage of prescription drugs, firearms, and dangerous weapons in homes or public spaces; and
WHEREAS
, according to a report by the U.S. CDC, there were 181 deaths by firearms in the State of Maine in 2024, with over 86 percent of the deaths the result of suicide; and
WHEREAS
, in 2025, there were 390 confirmed and suspected fatal drug overdoses, 20.4 percent lower than the total confirmed fatal overdoses for 2024; and
WHEREAS
, by ensuring that firearms and prescription drugs are properly stored and secured, this law will reduce accidental gun deaths, prevent suicide, and improve public health; and
WHEREAS
, in accordance with 1 MRSA § 150-R, the month of September of each year is designated as Safe Homes Awareness Month to raise awareness of the importance of safety in the home and the assistance that is available through the Safe Homes Program established in Title 25, section 7001;
NOW, THEREFORE
, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim September 2026 as
Safe Homes Awareness Month
throughout the State of Maine, and I urge all citizens to recognize this observance, promote the proper storage of prescription drugs and firearms, and learn more about the assistance available through the Safe Homes Program.

Notice of Agency Rulemaking Proposal

 

AGENCY: Department of Health and Human Services, Office of MaineCare Services, Division of Policy

CHAPTER NUMBER AND RULE TITLE: 10-144 C.M.R. Ch. 101, MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM), Ch. III, Sec. 20, Allowances for Home and Community-Based Services for Adults with Other Related Conditions

TYPE OF RULE: Major Substantive

BRIEF SUMMARY: Section 20 in the MBM authorizes home and community-based services (HCBS) under a CMS-approved Section 1915(c) waiver. The Department proposes to amend the Chapter III, Section 20 rule to establish the reimbursement methodology for new services being added under a companion, Chapter II, Section 20 rule, and to remove rates of reimbursement for all services which will now be listed in Rate Schedules on the Department’s website pursuant to 22 M.R.S. § 3177-J. The website address for current rates of reimbursement in the Department’s website and the statutory authority for this approach is stated in this proposed rule. Procedure codes, modifiers, and billable units remain in the rule, together with provisions for annual cost of living adjustments in conformance with 22 M.R.S. § 3173-J(2)(D)(3). Such cost-of-living adjustments will satisfy the requirements for direct support worker wages set forth in 22 M.R.S. § 7402(1).

See http://www.maine.gov/dhhs/oms/rules/index.shtml for rules and related rulemaking documents.

Once adopted, the proposed Chapter III, Section 20 rule will only be provisional: as a major substantive rule, Chapter III, Section 20 requires Legislative approval before it can be legally effective. Therefore, the Department anticipates also adopting an emergency Chapter III, Section 20 rule so that these methodology and rates changes will become legally effective on the same date as changes to the Chapter II, Section 20 routine technical rule becomes effective.

Through this rulemaking the Department proposes to: align similar processes, new services, service descriptions, definitions, and provider requirements with Maine’s four other Section 1915(c) waivers; make permanent certain flexibilities first utilized for Section 20 services during the Covid-19 Public Health Emergency (PHE); strengthen safeguards for Members by enacting the Plan of Corrective Action and Request for Exceptions processes; and incorporate the Department’s Global HCBS Rule (MBM Ch. Additionally, the Department proposes to require ` Section 20 providers to comply with 10-149 C.M.R. ch. 1, sec. 2-Grievances once this new grievance rule is adopted pursuant to the Maine Administrative Procedure Act (APA). The Department is concurrently undertaking major substantive rulemaking under the APA for MBM Ch. III, Sec. 20, to establish reimbursement procedures for the new and updated services described in this rulemaking.
